name: South Sudan
prevalence_note: South Sudan's telecom regulator NCA runs SS-CIRT as the national cyber-incident focal point and lists phishing among common threats; public warnings in 2026 centre on mobile-money account takeover and WhatsApp links that copy state bodies.
cross_border_note: Contact is usually in English or Juba Arabic, by voice call, SMS or WhatsApp, and may borrow the look of MTN MoMo, a Zain service or a government body.

scams.name: Mobile-money PIN or verification-code takeover

red_flag_keywords.text: give me the code that just came to your phone
your MoMo will be blocked today
tell me your PIN to fix the account

scams.signals_en: Someone presenting as wallet or network staff says the South Sudan mobile-money line has a fault and asks for the PIN or a code that just arrived, which lets them take over the wallet.
scams.legit_en: NCA guidance urges users to protect accounts and report suspicious contact; SS-CIRT advice says anyone who disclosed a PIN or code should contact the bank or wallet provider directly through its published care channel.
bait_tactics: The Juba network is weak here and no code message has come in on this SIM.
This phone belongs to my cousin, and the MoMo line is registered under a different handset.

scams.name: Fake state registration link on WhatsApp
scams.name_en: Fake state registration link on WhatsApp

red_flag_keywords.text: register online and the card is delivered free
upload your ID through this link

scams.signals_en: A forwarded WhatsApp note claims a national body is running online registration with free card delivery and pushes a short link that collects identity documents and personal details.
scams.legit_en: SS-CIRT and the elections commission point people to the official nec.gov.ss portal and physical registration points; suspicious links are reported to SS-CIRT without sending passwords or ID copies.
bait_tactics: The link does not load on this old phone, and the data bundle ran out this morning.
